title: Derived Hom formula for a dg quotient
statement:
Fix universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a small dg category over $\mathbf Z$, meaning a set of objects, cochain complexes $\mathcal C(X,Y)$, closed degree-zero units and associative unital chain-map composition. Let $\mathcal A\subset\mathcal C$ be a full dg subcategory (a subset of the objects, with unchanged mapping complexes). Use cochains and their derived category as in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived enrichment as in [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification]. The dg quotient $j:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C/\mathcal A$ exists: it has, up to equivalence, the images of the objects of $\mathcal C$ and is universal among derived enriched functors making every object of $\mathcal A$ contractible (its identity zero in $H^0$), including the enhanced functor categories and their transformations. For $X,Y\in\mathcal C$, put $h_Y(A)=\mathcal C(A,Y)$ and $h^X(A)=\mathcal C(X,A)$, respectively right and left dg $\mathcal A$-modules with actions by composition. A right module consists of complexes $G(A)$ and unital associative chain-map actions $G(B)\otimes\mathcal A(A,B)\to G(A)$; a left module consists of complexes $F(A)$ and actions $\mathcal A(A,B)\otimes F(A)\to F(B)$ with the same unit and associativity requirements. There is a natural cofiber sequence in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$
$$h_Y\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal A}h^X\longrightarrow\mathcal C(X,Y)\longrightarrow(\mathcal C/\mathcal A)(jX,jY).$$
The first arrow is evaluation by composition and the second is induced by $j$. Here the underived tensor of a right module $G$ and left module $F$ is the quotient complex of $\bigoplus_{A\in\mathcal A}G(A)\otimes F(A)$ by the relations $(ga)\otimes f=g\otimes(af)$; $\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal A}$ is its derived tensor, computed on semi-free replacements, and depends only on the objectwise quasi-isomorphism classes of both inputs. A semi-free module is an increasing union starting at zero of dg submodules with coproducts of shifted representables as successive quotients. The displayed cofiber is the class of the mapping cone; its identification with the quotient mapping object is compatible with the quotient map and natural in both variables. No flatness of the original mapping complexes over $\mathbf Z$ is assumed.

If $\mathcal C$ is pretriangulated, meaning its representable dg modules are closed up to homotopy equivalence under zero, shifts and mapping cones, and $\mathcal A$ contains zero and is closed under shifts and cones, then $j$ presents the enhanced localization at closed degree-zero maps whose cones are homotopy equivalent to objects of $\mathcal A$. Enhanced localization means universality for inverting these maps on enriched functor categories, including all coherent transformations as in [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal].

source.place: Drinfeld, DG quotients of DG categories, sections 1.3.1-1.3.3 (canonical cone formula), 1.6.2 (universal property), 2.4 (pretriangulated categories), 3.1 and 3.5-3.6 (flat replacement before adjoining contractions), 14.3 and 14.8 (tensor and semi-free resolutions); compare Keller, On differential graded categories, section 4.4, Theorems 4.7-4.8 and refined universal properties, printed pp. 16-17. Read online; no Stacks tag states this general dg-quotient formula.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure] to obtain an identity-on-objects cofibrant replacement $p:\mathcal C_c\to\mathcal C$. Let $\mathcal A_c$ be the full subcategory on the objects of $\mathcal A$. Thus $p|_{\mathcal A_c}$ is an identity-on-objects quasi-equivalence and all mapping complexes of $\mathcal C_c$, hence of $\mathcal A_c$, are homotopically flat. Over $\mathcal C_c$ freely adjoin, simultaneously for $A\in\mathcal A_c$, generators $\varepsilon_A:A\to A$ of degree $-1$ with $d\varepsilon_A=1_A$, and call the resulting dg category $Q$. The free-cell construction [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus] supplies the word composition and filtration; for several generators iterate the attachment and take the colimit over finite subsets. It creates no objects. The differential squares to zero because it does so on the original morphisms and on each generator, and its Leibniz extension is a derivation. The quotient arrow $j$ will be the derived enriched composite $\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal C_c\to Q$, using [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification]; it need not be a strict functor from the unreplaced dg category.

source.place: Drinfeld §§3.1, 3.5 and 13.5; homotopically flat replacement is made before adjoining any contraction.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-dg-free-cell-mapping-fibre] with $n_A=-1$ and $z_A=1_A$. For a strict $F:\mathcal C_c\to\mathcal E$, the homotopy fibre of restriction from $Q$ is the product, over $A$, of paths from zero to $1_{F(A)}$ in $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)}(\mathbf Z,\mathcal E(F(A),F(A)))$. If $F(A)$ is not contractible this path space is empty. If $d h_A=1_{F(A)}$, left multiplication $u\mapsto h_Au$ contracts the entire endomorphism complex, since $d(h_Au)+h_A d(u)=u$. Hence that mapping space, and the path fibre between its two points, is contractible. It follows that restriction on dg-category mapping spaces is an equivalence onto the union of components of functors annihilating every $A$. This proves existence and uniqueness with all homotopies of extensions at the level of mapping spaces, rather than inferring it from a strict correspondence of functors and chosen contractions.

source.place: Drinfeld §1.6, Keller §4.4 refined universal properties; explicit free-cell fibre computation.

proof.text: We now recover entire enriched functor categories. By [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus] and [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification], for each small enriched category $\mathcal J$ we may use a dg model of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal J,\mathcal E)$ as target in Step 2 and curry the result. An object of this functor category is contractible exactly when all its values are contractible. Indeed the full enriched subcategory $\mathcal E_0$ of contractible objects has zero mapping objects: in a dg model, multiplication by a contraction of the target contracts every Hom complex into it. If nonempty $\mathcal E_0$ is equivalent to the one-object category with zero mapping complex, so every diagram in it is contractible; if it is empty only an empty-domain diagram is possible, and that functor category is the same one-object zero category. Full-subcategory factorization and currying from the tensor-calculus node show the converse by evaluation and show that diagrams with contractible values factor through $\mathcal E_0$. Consequently the mapping-space result for every $\mathcal J$ identifies $\operatorname{Map}(\mathcal J,\operatorname{Fun}(Q,\mathcal E))$ with the mapping space into the full enriched subcategory of $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C_c,\mathcal E)$ on functors annihilating $\mathcal A_c$. These tests imply an equivalence of those enriched categories: test with each of the two categories to construct an inverse and check the two inverse identities. Thus restriction retains noninvertible transformations as well as all higher homotopies. Transport along $p$ gives precisely the enhanced annihilation universal property stated for $j$.

source.place: Keller §4.4 refined properties and §4.3 (internal Hom); the argument tests all enriched parameters instead of upgrading only degree-zero transformations.

proof.text: For later descent record explicitly the tensor comparison for $v=p|_{\mathcal A_c}$. Let $G$ be a right dg $\mathcal A$-module and $F$ a left dg $\mathcal A$-module. Derived tensor is computed by either semi-free input, with invariance in both inputs, by [lem-coef-dg-two-sided-bar-derived-tensor]. Choose a semi-free left resolution $P\to v^*F$ using [lem-coef-dg-module-semi-free-replacement] on the opposite category. Define $v_!P$ by extension of scalars, the coend $\mathcal A(v(-),-)\otimes_{\mathcal A_c}P$. The coend relations give an adjunction and send a representable at $A$ to the representable at $vA$, by evaluation $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$ with inverse $c\mapsto c\otimes1_A$. Extension preserves the graded-split semi-free filtration. The unit $P\to v^*v_!P$ is an objectwise quasi-isomorphism: on each successive quotient it is a direct sum of shifts of the mapping-complex quasi-isomorphisms for $v$; the cone of the unit on each filtration quotient is therefore acyclic. For a degreewise exact extension of two acyclic complexes, lift a primitive of the image of a cycle in the quotient and subtract its differential; the residual cycle lies in the acyclic subcomplex and is again a boundary. Induction makes every finite filtration stage of the unit cone acyclic; every cycle in its union lies in such a stage and is a boundary there. This proves the assertion without any convergence assumption. The adjoint $v_!P\to F$ is therefore a quasi-isomorphism, since its restriction composed with the unit is $P\to v^*F$, and $v$ has the same object set. Finally the balanced relations give $G\otimes_{\mathcal A}v_!P\cong v^*G\otimes_{\mathcal A_c}P$. Applying the cited semi-free tensor comparison gives a natural identification of derived tensors over $\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal A_c$. This argument establishes the necessary base-change comparison without citing a module-model theorem whose proof depends on this item.

source.place: Drinfeld §§14.3-14.4, 14.8-14.12 and 2.7; filtration proof of the identity-on-objects quasi-equivalence comparison.

proof.text: Put $G_c(A)=\mathcal C_c(A,Y)$ and $F_c(A)=\mathcal C_c(X,A)$. Step 1 makes both modules objectwise homotopically flat and all mapping complexes of $\mathcal A_c$ homotopically flat. Thus [lem-coef-dg-two-sided-bar-derived-tensor] supplies $B=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}V_n[n]$ as their derived tensor. By [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus], the length-zero summand of $Q(X,Y)$ is $\mathcal C_c(X,Y)$; its length-$n+1$ summand is the tensor $V_n$ interleaved with $n+1$ degree-$-1$ contraction generators. These direct sums are graded decompositions, not decompositions into subcomplexes.

source.place: Drinfeld §§3.1 and 3.6(i): unnormalized word/bar differential; the quotient includes its length-zero summand.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-interleaved-tensor-suspension] on every tuple of intermediate objects and take the direct sum. It identifies $B[1]$ with the positive-length graded summands by
$$\Phi_n(a_0\otimes\cdots\otimes a_{n+1})=(-1)^{n+\sum_j(n+1-j)|a_j|}a_0\varepsilon_{A_n}a_1\cdots a_n\varepsilon_{A_0}a_{n+1}.$$
The lemma identifies the length-preserving internal differential with $(-1)^{n+1}d_{V_n}$, exactly the internal part of $-d_B$ from [lem-coef-dg-two-sided-bar-derived-tensor]. There is no use of a flatness assumption in this sign comparison.

source.place: Drinfeld §§3.1 and 3.6(i): unnormalized word/bar differential; the quotient includes its length-zero summand.

proof.text:
The Leibniz differential of [lem-coef-dgcat-free-cell-calculus] has, besides the internal terms, only terms deleting one contraction because $d\varepsilon_A=1_A$. Apply [lem-coef-contraction-word-bar-faces] to these terms. In bar degree $n\geq1$ it gives $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^{i+1}\partial_i$, the negative of the bar-face differential in [lem-coef-dg-two-sided-bar-derived-tensor]; in bar degree zero it gives composition with sign $+1$. Hence under $\mathrm{id}\oplus\Phi$ the full word differential on $\mathcal C_c(X,Y)\oplus B[1]$ is
$$\begin{pmatrix}d_{\mathcal C_c}&\mathrm{ev}\\0&-d_B\end{pmatrix},$$
where evaluation is composition on $V_0$ and zero on higher bar degrees. This is the defining mapping-cone differential. Inclusion of the length-zero summand is the word quotient functor's map, so its cone triangle has both canonical arrows required in the statement.

source.place: Drinfeld §§3.1 and 3.6(i): unnormalized word/bar differential; the quotient includes its length-zero summand.

proof.text: The maps $G_c\to v^*h_Y$ and $F_c\to v^*h^X$ induced by $p$ are objectwise quasi-isomorphisms. The invariance and naturality in [lem-coef-dg-two-sided-bar-derived-tensor], followed by the comparison of Step 4, identify $B$ with $h_Y\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal A}h^X$. The morphism $\mathcal C_c(X,Y)\to\mathcal C(X,Y)$ is also a quasi-isomorphism. All these maps commute with evaluation because $p(gf)=p(g)p(f)$; hence the cone triangle from Steps 5–7 becomes exactly the displayed cofiber sequence of the statement, with its first arrow evaluation and its second arrow induced by $j$. Precomposition in $X$ and postcomposition in $Y$ act on every word and every bar factor and commute with the Leibniz differential, so the comparison is natural in both variables. Semi-free tensor invariance gives independence of input resolutions; the enhanced universal property of Step 3 identifies different quotient models compatibly with their maps. No flatness of $\mathcal C$ was used: all underived bar computations took place over the locally flat replacement $\mathcal C_c$.

source.place: Drinfeld §§1.3.1-1.3.3, 3.5-3.6 and 14.8-14.12; compatibility with both arrows and both variables.

proof.text: Suppose $\mathcal C$ is pretriangulated. For any derived enriched $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$, choose a strict representative on a cofibrant replacement as allowed by [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure] and [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification]. Apply [lem-coef-dg-finite-twisted-extension] to extend it to finite twisted complexes. That node says that pretriangulated hulls preserve quasi-equivalences, contain the original categories fully faithfully, and that their induced homotopy-category functors are exact. Therefore $F(\operatorname{Cone}(f))$ is identified in the target hull with the formal cone of $F(f)$ even when $\mathcal E$ itself is not pretriangulated. By [lem-kun-distinguished-cone-zero], $F(f)$ is invertible if and only if that object is zero, equivalently its identity is a boundary in the target dg hull. Full faithfulness of the original target embedding identifies this with contractibility of $F(\operatorname{Cone}(f))$ in $\mathcal E$. If $F$ annihilates $\mathcal A$, this holds for every $f$ whose cone is homotopy equivalent to an object of $\mathcal A$. Conversely the zero object of $\mathcal C$ is preserved up to contractibility by the finite-twisted extension, and for each $A\in\mathcal A$ the map $0\to A$ has cone homotopy equivalent to $A$. Inverting these maps forces $F(A)$ contractible. Thus the two classes of functors are exactly the same. Their full enriched subcategories, including transformations, are equal. Step 3 and [lem-coef-enhanced-localization-universal] now identify $j$ with the enhanced localization at the indicated maps. We assert localization AT this class, not that the class lists every map inverted after saturation; closure under retracts is not assumed or needed.

source.place: Drinfeld §§2.4-2.5 and §1.6; Keller §4.5; cone-zero test in the target pretriangulated hull.

proof_origin.place: Drinfeld §§1.3, 1.6, 2.4-2.5, 3.1, 3.5-3.6, 13.5-13.6 and 14.3-14.12; Keller §§4.3-4.5 read online. Full enriched universality is obtained by parameter testing, not from a strict-functor correspondence.
